dialogue.transliteration: ee, kint a7chi wiyya akhuuy. aasif, ma gdarit ardd 3aleech
dialogue.english: Yeah, I was talking with my brother. Sorry, I couldn't answer you.

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab
dialogue.arabic: ما يخالف. أريد أحچي وياك عن الموعد
dialogue.transliteration: ma ykhaalif. ariid a7chi wiyyaak 3an il-maw3id

dialogue.transliteration: zeen, khal a7chi bsur3a gabul ma yingit3 il-khatt

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: لا، خلص، الخط انقطع. تقدرين تدقين عليّ بعد شوية؟
dialogue.transliteration: laa, khalaas, il-khatt ingita3. tigdariin tdiggiin 3aleyya ba3d shwayya?

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab

dialogue.transliteration: ee akiid, adugg 3aleek hassa

dialogue.speaker: Samer

dialogue.transliteration: allaah yislamich, antirich

pair.english: Can you call me back in a bit?

lessons.culture: Iraqis usually answer with «آلو» or «هلا» and ask «منو المتكلم؟», and the greeting «شكو ماكو؟» comes before any business, so diving straight in sounds abrupt. Phone credit is topped up with scratch cards from the mobile companies (Zain, Asiacell, Korek), so «رصيدي خلص» is a very common line.

exercises.prompt: The phone rings and you answer. Say hello and ask who is speaking.

lessons.culture: In Iraq friends often fix a meeting loosely, «بعد العصر» (after the afternoon prayer) or «بالليل», and a few minutes' lateness is usually shrugged off, which is why «لا تتأخر» is said with a smile. A cafe or a tea house (جايخانة) is the usual place to meet. The Umayyad Mosque is in Damascus, so in Baghdad people would name a local landmark instead, such as the Abu Hanifa Mosque in Adhamiyah.

dialogue.transliteration: ee, nilghii, w laazim a3tithir marra thaanya 3an it-taghyiir
dialogue.english: Yes, we cancel it, and I have to apologise again for the change.

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab

dialogue.transliteration: wala yhimmak. zeen innak khabbartni min is-subu7

dialogue.speaker: Samer

dialogue.transliteration: mashkuura, ashoofich baachir in shaa2 allaah

pair.english: I want to change the appointment.
Is the place still the same place?

lessons.culture: Iraqis soften a cancellation with a reason and an apology, and the expected answer is «ما يخالف» or «ولا يهمك», so refusing an apology would sound cold. A family or work reason is normally accepted without further questions, and «إن شاء الله» is usually added to the new time.

lessons.culture: Callers often open with «السلام عليكم» before asking for someone, and whoever answers, often a relative, replies «وعليكم السلام» and asks «منو المتكلم؟». Taking a message is a normal favour, and the answer is usually «إن شاء الله أقله» rather than a fixed promise.

exercises.tip: «كلش» means very or a lot.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: «رسالة / تقدر / تاخذلي».

too_formal.feedback: Correct Arabic, but this is the formal or written version, not what is said in Baghdad.

exercises.tip: «تاخذلي» is "take for me" in one word.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: «يوصل / أقله / ما / أول».

too_formal.feedback: Correct Arabic, but this is the formal or written version, not what is said in Baghdad.

exercises.tip: «أول ما» means as soon as.

challenge.title: A Phone Call to Rearrange Plans
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a phone conversation of at least 10 lines. It must include answering the phone, proposing a place and a time to meet, changing that plan for a real reason, agreeing on a new time or place, and, if the person you called is not free, leaving a message for someone else to pass on.
required_elements: Asking who is speaking, using منو المتكلم or آني + name.
A suggestion of where to meet, using خل نتلاقى or a similar phrase.
A question about time, using أي ساعة تناسبك or الساعة شكد.
A reason for changing the plan, using طلع عندي شغل or a similar phrase.
A request to postpone or change, using نقدر نأجل or أريد أغيّر الموعد.
An apology for the change, using آسف على هالتغيير المفاجئ or a similar phrase.
A reassurance in response, using ما يخالف or ولا يهمك.
A closing thank-you, using مشكور كلش.
At least one exchange about leaving or taking a message, using رسالة or قله.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: آلُو؟
dialogue.transliteration: aaloo?
dialogue.english: Hello?

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab
dialogue.arabic: هلا سامر، آني زينب. شكو ماكو؟
dialogue.transliteration: hala Saamer, aani Zaynab. shaku maaku?
dialogue.english: Hi Samer, it's Zaynab. What's new?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: ماكو شي، الحمد لله. شكو؟
dialogue.transliteration: maaku shi, il-7amdillah. shaku?
dialogue.english: Nothing much, thank God. What's up?

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab
dialogue.arabic: خل نتلاقى بالكافيه باچر. أي ساعة تناسبك؟
dialogue.transliteration: khal nitlaaga bil-kaafeeh baachir. ay saa3a tnaasbak?
dialogue.english: Let's meet at the cafe tomorrow. What time suits you?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: الساعة خمسة زينة إلي
dialogue.transliteration: is-saa3a khamsa zeena ili
dialogue.english: 5 o'clock is good for me.

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab
dialogue.arabic: تمام، أنطرك قدام المدخل الرئيسي
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, antirak gdaam il-madkhal ir-ra2iisi
dialogue.english: Great, I'll wait for you in front of the main entrance.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: آسف، طلع عندي شغل بالبيت وما أقدر أجي الساعة خمسة
dialogue.transliteration: aasif, tila3 3indi shughul bil-beet w ma agdar aji is-saa3a khamsa
dialogue.english: Sorry, something came up at home and I can't come at 5.

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab
dialogue.arabic: ما يخالف. نقدر نأجل للسبعة؟
dialogue.transliteration: ma ykhaalif. nigdar n2ajjil lis-sab3a?
dialogue.english: No problem. Can we postpone to 7?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: إي، نأجل للسبعة. آسف على هالتغيير المفاجئ
dialogue.transliteration: ee, n2ajjil lis-sab3a. aasif 3ala hal-taghyiir il-mufaaji2
dialogue.english: Yes, we postpone to 7. Sorry for the sudden change.

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك. وإذا ما رديت باچر، أخلي رسالة عند أخوك
dialogue.transliteration: wala yhimmak. w idha ma rdeit baachir, akhalli risaala 3ind akhuuk
dialogue.english: Don't worry. And if you don't answer tomorrow, I'll leave a message with your brother.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أكيد، وهو يخبرني. مشكور كلش على صبرك
dialogue.transliteration: akiid, w huwwa yikhabbirni. mashkuur kullish 3ala sabrak
dialogue.english: Sure, and he will let me know. Thanks a lot for your patience.

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab
dialogue.arabic: العفو، أشوفك الساعة سبعة
dialogue.transliteration: il-3afu, ashoofak is-saa3a sab3a
dialogue.english: You're welcome, see you at 7.
